prompt:
Find real, documented examples of open-source maintainers publicly reporting AI-generated bug reports or pull requests as a burden (e.g. curl, Python, other projects). Cite the original posts and quote what they said.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

If you're not sure about something, just say so.

response.content:
Based on the provided web search results, I have found multiple direct quotations from open-source maintainers documenting the burden of AI-generated bug reports. The most prominent example is Daniel Stenberg, the founder and lead developer of the `curl` project.

Here are the real, documented examples following the required format.

**Daniel Stenberg on the curl project:**

SOURCE: https://daniel.haxx.se/blog/2025/07/14/death-by-a-thousand-slops/ | QUOTE: "The general trend so far in 2025 has been way more AI slop than ever before (about 20% of all submissions) as we have averaged in about two security report submissions per week." | CLAIM: The lead developer of curl quantifies the volume of "AI slop" as a significant and growing percentage of all security submissions.

SOURCE: https://daniel.haxx.se/blog/2025/07/14/death-by-a-thousand-slops/ | QUOTE: "In early July, about 5% of the submissions in 2025 had turned out to be genuine vulnerabilities. The valid-rate has decreased significantly compared to previous years." | CLAIM: The quality of reports has plummeted, with the vast majority (95%) of submissions being invalid, wasting maintainer time.

SOURCE: https://daniel.haxx.se/blog/2025/07/14/death-by-a-thousand-slops/ | QUOTE: "Every report thus engages 3-4 persons. Perhaps for 30 minutes, sometimes up to an hour or three. Each." | CLAIM: Each invalid report consumes a significant amount of collective, volunteer time from the small security team.

SOURCE: https://daniel.haxx.se/blog/2025/07/14/death-by-a-thousand-slops/ | QUOTE: "Not to mention the emotional toll it takes to deal with these mind-numbing stupidities." | CLAIM: The burden is not just about time; it also has a negative emotional impact, contributing to burnout.

SOURCE: https://redmonk.com/videos/daniel-stenberg-ai-onslop/ | QUOTE: "is not only the volume goes up, the quality goes down. So we spend more time than ever to get less out of it than ever." | CLAIM: AI-generated reports create a double burden: higher volume and lower quality, maximizing the waste of maintainer effort.

SOURCE: https://redmonk.com/videos/daniel-stenberg-ai-onslop/ | QUOTE: "It is a little bit of abuse because most of these, that we call them AI slop, they’re just generated by someone really quickly... they just hand it over to us and we get a couple of hours of work per every such instance." | CLAIM: The maintainer characterizes low-effort AI reports as a form of abuse that unfairly transfers a large workload to the project team.

SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "Stenberg said the amount of time it takes project maintainers to triage each AI-assisted vulnerability report... is tantamount to a DDoS attack on the project." | CLAIM: The maintainer equates the flood of AI reports to a Denial-of-Service attack, emphasizing how it overwhelms project resources.

SOURCE: https://arstechnica.com/gadgets/2025/05/open-source-project-curl-is-sick-of-users-submitting-ai-slop-vulnerabilities/ | QUOTE: "“A threshold has been reached. We are effectively being DDoSed. If we could, we would charge them for this waste of our time,” wrote Daniel Stenberg" | CLAIM: A direct quote from the maintainer stating the problem has reached a critical level where it feels like an attack on the project.

**Seth Larson on the Python project:**

SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "Python's Seth Larson also raised concerns about these AI slop reports back in December, saying that responding to them is expensive and time-consuming because on face value, they seem legitimate and must be investigated further by trained eyes before confirming that they are, in fact, bogus." | CLAIM: A Python security maintainer confirms that AI reports are a widespread problem, consuming time because their initial appearance of legitimacy requires deep investigation.

SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "“Security reports that waste maintainers' time result in confusion, stress, frustration, and to top it off, a sense of isolation due to the secretive nature of security reports,” Larson wrote. "All of these feelings can add to burnout of likely highly trusted contributors to open source projects." | CLAIM: The Python maintainer details the psychological and emotional burden of these reports, linking them directly to contributor burnout.

**Other Projects (mentioned by Stenberg):**

SOURCE: https://lwn.net/Articles/1058266/ | QUOTE: "Stenberg said that once he started talking loudly about the AI slop, he heard from many other projects that had the same problem." | CLAIM: The `curl` maintainer indicates that the problem of AI-generated bug reports is not isolated to his project but is a widespread issue across the open-source ecosystem.

NO_SOURCE_FOUND: A specific, direct quote from a maintainer of a project other than curl or Python (e.g., for a Linux distribution, a JavaScript library, etc.) publicly reporting AI-generated pull requests as a burden. The search results confirm the problem exists broadly but do not provide a specific quote from another project's maintainer.
